Fruit Love Island (@ai.cinema021) and @frutystory creators: press-level process only (scriptwriting, scene planning, redo loops); no line-level evidence published.

Single-tester numbers (eastondev lip-sync success rates; Ambience word budgets) are practitioner evidence, not benchmarks — B-12 is flagged rather than asserted for this reason.

lines: Clippie publishes the genre's script contract: 'Name: line', one line per scene, bracketed acting tags [whispers]/[gasps] performed not read, ~5.5 s per line, one-page character bible + 2-3 recurring conflicts.
Draft double, cut half: Gigi M. Green via OpenMicroDrama — write 20 lines, cut 10; no more than 10 lines an episode; write the cliffhanger first.
One complication / exactly one reversal per 60-s episode (Oakgen; InVideo); the hanger swap test — a cliffhanger swappable onto another episode is decoration (drama.so).
On the TTS route the scene is performed as ONE take; line-by-line generation is the named cause of robotic dialogue (Paintbrush / Eleven v4 Text to Dialogue).
Naturalness is briefed as intention + the withheld line ('what each character wants, and what they are avoiding saying'), never requested as a quality (Debutify / MiniMax H3 practice).
prompts: Field rendering convention is per-model: label + colon/says + quoted line (Sora 2 official Dialogue block; Higgsfield library), Kling tone-parenthesis + bare line, Seedance {} braces — the script's colon form is the script layer, the wrapper is MODEL_SYNTAX.
Test-based comfort budgets sit below our F-25 ceiling: Ambience's Seedance tests ~20 words/15 s with garbling tracking LINE length (21-word quote -> phoneme soup); Veo guides 6-12 words per 8-s clip.
Listener-silence is a prescribed prompt sentence in three independent sources ('listens silently, mouth closed') to stop both faces mouthing one line.
Speaking is the only action: one verb per character per sentence; a speaking character gets no simultaneous second action (shared-action failure is the named multi-character bug).
Names in prompt prose get rendered as on-screen text (Seedance) or spoken (Veo) — name hygiene is a prompt-layer rule, and prompt-enhancement/rewriting must be off for exact lines.
